summary: Design practical MEAL systems for adaptive, multi-partner programmes. Build evidence tools, learning agendas, and dashboards. Enquire today.
lede: Adaptive MEAL training helps programme professionals design evidence systems for complex humanitarian and development work. It is for practitioners responsible for monitoring, evaluation, accountability, learning or programme decisions, and covers building indicator hierarchies, checking partner data quality, and prioritizing learning questions. Participants also practise using feedback and contribution analysis to connect evidence with adaptive management decisions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already contribute to programme monitoring, evaluation, accountability, learning, reporting, or adaptive management. It suits practitioners who need to design or strengthen MEAL systems across complex, multi-partner humanitarian and development programmes.
audience: Programme Managers using evidence to adjust humanitarian
modules: Theory of Change and MEAL Architecture
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to programme implementation, monitoring, evaluation, accountability, learning, or donor reporting. No coding or programming is required. Familiarity with a results framework, basic spreadsheet use, and routine programme reporting will help you contribute effectively. Advanced evaluation methods such as contribution analysis, Outcome Harvesting, and Most Significant Change receive operational application rather than technical research implementation depth.
